newsitem.title: GERMANY: Show Germany "as it is" Kohl tells Expo 2000 team.
newsitem.headline: Show Germany "as it is" Kohl tells Expo 2000 team.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Wednesday he wants Germany shown "as it really is" by a world fair, Expo 2000, in the northern city of Hanover in four years' time.
"I want the Expo and I want it to be a success," Kohl told reporters ahead of a meeting with some 40 leading industrialists to try to boost industry's financial commitment to the event.

"If there is one thing I am committed to with all my attention and sympathy, then this is it," he said, calling the planned event a chance "to show Germany to the world as it really is, with all its strengths and weaknesses, and without arrogance."

The meeting came amid signs that the 2.8 billion mark ($1.84 billion) event has been slow to inspire both industrial backers and some major economic powers such as Japan and the United States, neither of which is among the 83 countries signed up so far.
The German industry federation BDI has complained of a lack of clear planning for the centrepieces of the Expo, the 50-million-mark German pavilion and the central theme park.
Kohl said it was rare for large numbers of backers to sign up for a project so early in its development, and that he was convinced sufficient backing would be found.
Organisers expect the fair, whose theme is "People-Nature-Technology", to attract around 40 million visitors between June 1 and October 31, 2000.
